coherence.why: Stays on number line fractions but jumps abruptly from chocolate to 2/5 activity, then road/tea shop example; repeats identical card many times unasked.

follows_child.why: Child shares drawing, peacock, sister spilling milk, Shekhar/cricket stories but teacher gives minimal nods then redirects without follow-up on interests.

understanding.why: Teacher claims grasp after repeats but misses confusion ('pata nahi', word choice uncertainty); parent summary notes uncertainty, teach-back not passed.

adapts.why: On confusion about game/screen and 'pata nahi', repeats same 2/5 card and gap-counting prompt instead of any new explanation method.

human.why: Warm Hinglish ('Bilkul', 'Koi baat nahi Riya'), ties briefly to tiger drawing; natural tone though some lines feel repetitive.

channel_truth.why: Repeats identical question card/board for 2/5 unasked; says 'game mein rakhiye' and 'khaali jagah bhariye' while child sees only 'play' button on voice-first screen.

safety_floor.why: Casual stories about spills and cricket; no distress, harm, low mood or safety disclosure at any point.

pacing.why: Frequent questions suit chatty 5th grader but long stuck loop on one comparison (turns 4-9) prevents covering greater-than-1 fractions.

judged.verdict: Riya got some practice counting gaps for fractions like 2/5, 1/6 and 1/4 but the teacher repeated the same screen and question too many times, ignored her drawing and Shekhar stories, and never reached fractions greater than 1.

follows_child.why: Never answers 'fractions kya hota hai'; ignores repeated requests for the correct phrase ('left of' vs 'to the left of'); when child says the screen only shows 'play', teacher gives mechanical instructions instead of resolving the confusion.

understanding.why: Claims 'pakad liya' and 'exact method / bilkul sahi method' despite the child's tentative guessing and self-correcting; never detects that understanding is only partial.

adapts.why: When child is stuck on wording, teacher repeats the same fill-in-the-blank prompt or switches to an unexplained game; later repeats the same six-gaps question verbatim instead of re-explaining.

human.why: Hinglish register is age-appropriate and the cricket aside shows some warmth, but frequent templated repetitions and robotic re-reading of card text make the interaction feel scripted.

pacing.why: Several turns stall on the same 'left of the middle' wording and the 1/6 question, creating a stuck loop; otherwise the progression is roughly acceptable for the age.
